item.description: World leaders on Tuesday (local time) have extended prayers and wishes for the speedy recovery of Pope Leo XIV following his successful lung surgery at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, expressing hope for his ...
item.content:encoded:
World leaders unite in prayers for Pope Leo XIV’s speedy recovery after successful lung surgery World leaders on Tuesday (local time) have extended prayers and wishes for the speedy recovery of Pope Leo XIV following his successful lung surgery at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, expressing hope for his return to health and highlighting his message of peace, humanity, unity and compassion amid his treatment for lung adenocarcinoma. ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 09:52 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 09:52 IST

Pope Leo XIV (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

World leaders on Tuesday (local time) extended prayers and wishes for the speedy recovery of Pope Leo XIV following his successful lung surgery at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, expressing hope for his return to health and highlighting his message of peace, humanity, unity and compassion amid his treatment for lung adenocarcinoma. The prayers come as the head of the Catholic Church recovers after doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung following a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio were among those who conveyed their prayers and wishes for the pontiff's recovery through posts on X. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described Pope Leo XIV as a source of inspiration for Catholics worldwide, emphasising his message of peace and humanity. "Pope Leo XIV is a source of inspiration to Catholics right around the world – and here in Australia. He is a voice for peace, humanity and reason in our modern world. My thoughts and prayers are with him as he recovers from his recent surgery. We hope and pray for a quick recovery," Albanese said in his post. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also conveyed his wishes for the Pope's recovery, underlining the significance of his message of unity and compassion. "On behalf of Canadians, I wish Pope Leo XIV a full and swift recovery following his successful surgery. His Holiness is a source of hope and inspiration for billions around the world. His message of unity and compassion reminds us of the strength we can offer one another in moments of uncertainty. As he recovers, may he draw strength from the prayers of those whose lives he has touched, just as so many draw strength from him," Carney said. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres also joined the global outpouring of prayers for the pontiff, wishing him a speedy recovery following his recent diagnosis. "Wishing His Holiness Pope Leo XIV a speedy recovery following his recent diagnosis. My prayers & thoughts are with @Pontifex & the Catholic community worldwide," Guterres said in his post. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed his prayers for the Pope's health, invoking divine guidance for the medical team overseeing his treatment. "Jeanette and I are united in prayer for @PONTIFEX’s health following his recent diagnosis. May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father," Rubio said. The US Conference of Catholic Bishops also confirmed the successful removal of a cancerous tumour from the Pope's right lung, calling on the faithful to continue praying for his recovery and for those affected by cancer. "Doctors at Gemelli Hospital removed a cancerous tumor from Pope Leo XIV’s right lung, according to the Holy See Press Office. The surgery was successful, with no complications, and the Holy Father has returned to his hospital room. We ask the faithful to continue praying for Pope Leo’s recovery and for the doctors and staff caring for him. We also hold in prayer all who are living with cancer, their families, and those who care for them," the US Conference of Catholic Bishops said in a post on X. According to Vatican News, Pope Leo XIV underwent thoracic surgery at Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, following preoperative examinations that confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. A statement from the Holy See Press Office said the procedure was carried out as planned, with doctors removing the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung using a video-assisted technique. “To ensure a radical resection, the lower lobe of his right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique. An intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as suspected from the preoperative examinations,” the statement read. The Holy See Press Office confirmed that the operation was successful and that no complications occurred. The Pope spent approximately three hours in the operating room, with the surgery itself lasting around 90 minutes. “The operation was successful, and there were no complications,” the statement added. Vatican News reported that Pope Leo awoke normally after the procedure and returned to his room on the hospital's 10th floor following a brief period of observation. According to Matteo Bruni, Director of the Holy See Press Office, the Pope asked for dinner after the operation and spent the evening with his secretaries and other Vatican staff. The surgical team was led by Professor Stefano Margaritora, assisted by Professor Elisa Meacci, Dr Maria Teresa Congedo and Dr Leonardo Petracca Ciavarella. The anaesthesia team comprised Professor Massimo Antonelli, Dr Giovanni Punzo and Dr Giuseppe Bello. Further examinations of the removed tissue are expected to be conducted in the coming days, Vatican News reported. Preoperative tests had helped doctors determine the location of the affected tissue and the appropriate surgical approach. (ANI)

item.title: Duane “Keffe D” Davis sentenced to 40 years of life imprisonment for orchestrating murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur
item.description: Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement.
item.content:encoded:
Duane “Keffe D” Davis sentenced to 40 years of life imprisonment for orchestrating murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement.  ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 09:51 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 09:51 IST

Duane “Keffe D” Davis faces sentence for Tupac Shakur murder (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

30 years after the death of rap icon Tupac Shakur in 1996, Duane “Keffe D” Davis has been sentenced to 40 years to life in a Nevada prison for orchestrating the killing, reported Variety. On Tuesday, Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement. Davis was facing a maximum of life in prison without parole. Prior to the judge’s decision, prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo pointed out a history of criminal activity and suggested that Davis “earned” the maximum sentence. “He’s an eight-time felon sitting before you on this crime perpetrated upon these family members, these family members, brothers. And you have to ask yourself, for this crime, for this person, what sentence does he deserve? Whatever your decision is, ultimately, in my mind, he deserves the maximum possible sentence because he’s earned it through his actions, his behaviour, and who he is as he stands here today,” he said, as quoted by Variety. Before handing down the sentence, Judge Carli Kierny went on to address Davis. “You don’t get to take a man from his family, you don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur. The world never forgot about him and his death, and you are going to face justice,” Kierny said, as quoted by People. Davis’ defence attorney Michael Sanft further claimed that they would appeal the judge’s decision, while Davis addressed the judge, asking for his “stuff back” that was taken from his home. In court, the late rapper’s sister, Sekyiwa Shakur and brother Maurice Shakur urged the judge to sentence Davis to the maximum punishment. “Tupac is truly my shining star, my shining prince; he is who God trusted to take care of me. My mother had two children, and God gave him to me, and he’s supposed to be my life partner. I spent 30 years without my protection. I believe that if any life mattered, if all life matters, for sure this man’s life mattered. I do believe when you take a life like that, you deserve every minute, every minute, of the maximum amount of punishment, time to sit down and contemplate what you’ve done to this world. He had so much promise, intentions for a better world for our people; he had plans and manifestos. He’s so much more than street violence,” Sekyiwa said as she struggled holding back tears. In late August, Davis was found guilty of murder with use of a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang. He was convicted after a weeks-long trial in Las Vegas, with prosecutors and police claiming that he orchestrated Shakur’s murder in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996. It was alleged that Davis handed the murder weapon to the gunman, believed to be either Davis’ nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson or another man in the car's back seat. Tupac Shakur was murdered in 1996 at a red light in Paradise, Nevada. He was shot four times, following which he succumbed to his injuries six days later. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
ＦＲＢ当局者、金利上昇が一部金融機関に課題もたらすと認識＝ボストン連銀総裁 6:17 配信

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）ビル。2025年9月撮影。REUTERS/Ken Cedeno

[１３日　ロイター] - 米ボストン地区連銀のコリンズ総裁は１３日、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）当局者は金利上昇が一部の金融機関に問題をもたらす可能性があることを認識していると述べた。

コリンズ総裁は同地区連銀での会議で「政策当局者としてわれわれは、金利の上昇が機会をもたらす一方で、いくつかの課題ももたらすことを十分に認識しており、その点について警戒し、留意していきたい」と語った。

また、金融政策のスタンスが変化する中で「適切に運営される銀行は、そうした側面について包括的に考える必要がある」と述べた。

さらに総裁は、インフレデータの動向に注目しており、インフレ圧力がどの程度広範に及んでいるかを注視していると述べた。

Apple's HomeView brings personalized Siri to smart home, takes on Amazon and Google

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 13 : Apple on Tuesday unveiled a smart-home hub that taps iPhone user data to make Siri more personal, but promised privacy safeguards designed to keep that information out of the company's hands. The HomeView smart-home hub, which took center stage at an event in New York, is an important test of Apple's AI strategy as it tries to close the gap with rivals Amazon and Alphabet's Google, while reinforcing its reputation for user privacy. In a series of demonstrations, Apple showed Siri AI recognizing a user's face and performing personalized tasks such as fetching recipes from text messages, finding a nearby farmer's market for missing ingredients and then updating shopping lists.  When a different member of the household steps in, the HomeView recognizes that user's face and switches to their personal data, for example fetching information from text messages about when a friend's early morning flight lands and how long it will take them to arrive, then teeing up a coffee maker a few minutes ahead of time.

The new device and Siri AI lean on the iPhone to make those personalized features happen, reflecting new CEO John Ternus' vision of Apple's best-selling product as an "intelligent personal hub" laid out at Apple's iPhone launch event last month.  Siri AI's usefulness hinges on how much it knows about a user. HomeView draws on a personal search index stored on the user's iPhone to personalize responses. "That will give you what's more relevant, what's more timely, what's important to you, because it's coming from your iPhone," Kaiann Drance, Apple's vice president of product marketing for home products, said in an interview. PRIVACY SAFEGUARDS AND ENCRYPTION HomeView has its own operating system and runs on Apple's A18 chip, designed to process encrypted user data in a walled-off part of the chip. To access private data, a user's iPhone has to be connected to the same home network as HomeView, and no private data is stored on the HomeView device itself. Apple said none of the data is used for marketing, including first-party advertising efforts. "One of the things we talked about is not building a marketing profile," Drance said. "Our intent is to provide users a helpful experience that adheres to simplicity, being personal, being intelligent, and continuing our commitment to privacy." A key difference between Siri AI and rival systems is that it does not end each interaction with a follow-up question designed to elicit more information from the user, a practice that Lilian Rincon, vice president of product marketing for AI, said was a deliberate choice on Apple's part.  "For us, it's really about creating these really great products for consumers, which is why we're not in this game of getting you to engage and continue the conversation in many, many, many turns," Rincon said. HomeView also required Apple to figure out how to make Siri personal on a device shared by multiple people in communal spaces such as a kitchen. Apple demonstrated HomeView juggling requests from family members during the morning rush to school and work. While the device can recognize up to six voices and faces to show private data, Apple said it will make decisions on which user to prioritize based on who last touched the device and other factors, and that some features such as weather and thermostat controls will be available to any user. "There is a logic built in to kind of manage that experience," Drance said. "There was thought put into the nature of that communal computer sharing of the voice and the face recognition."

Source: Reuters

item.content:encoded:
原油先物まちまち、米ロの軽油合意巡る期待と中東情勢懸念が交錯 5:41 配信

オマーン沿岸沖を航行する石油タンカー。オマーン・ムサンダムから６月撮影。REUTERS/Stringer

Scott DiSavino

[１３日　ロイター] - 米国時間の原油先物はまちまち。米ロのディーゼル（軽油）合意でロシアからの供給拡大への期待が広がる一方、サウジアラビアとイエメンでの攻撃が供給の一段の混乱を招くとの懸念が意識された。

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が前日比０．９６ドル（０．９％）安の１バレル＝１０５．６９ドル。前日は９月１５日以来の高値を付けていた。米ＷＴＩ先物は０．４０ドル（０．４％）高の９４．１４ドルと、９月２４日以来の高値で取引を終えた。

ロシア大統領府（クレムリン）は、ロシアが米国と世界市場にディーゼル（軽油）を供給するとトランプ米大統領が発表した合意について、ウクライナ和平協議に対するロシアの立場とは直接的な関連はないとの見解を示した。 ロシアとウクライナの戦争を終結させる合意が成立すれば、ロシアはエネルギーの輸出を拡大できる可能性がある。

一方、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は１３日、サウジアラビアが首都サヌアを攻撃していると発表。これに先立ち、サウジアラビア主導の連合軍は、サヌアにあるイエメン石油会社のサバハ中央給油所について、安全確保のため周辺住民に退避するよう呼びかけていた。

item.title: Bank of America fined $1.2 billion by US government for failing to police suspicious activity
item.description: Bank of America has been fined $1.21 billion by US regulators for widespread failures to detect potential money laundering and other illicit activity, a penalty the bank said will hurt third-quarter earnings.
item.dc:creator: Pete Schroeder, Ismail Shakil, Saeed Azhar
item.content:encoded: Bank of America (BAC.N) has been fined $1.21 billion by US regulators for widespread failures to detect potential money laundering and other illicit activity, a penalty the bank said will hurt third-quarter earnings. The Treasury Department said the fine, the third-largest in department history, is due to the bank's failure to report more than $5 billion in suspicious activity to the government, including $1 billion that posed national security-related and other priority illicit finance risks. "Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our economic and national security," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. "When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire US financial system to significant illicit finance risks." The Treasury said the bank "prioritized its revenues" in building compliance programs, and overly relied on inquiries from outside parties like law enforcement and other financial institutions instead of its own internal controls. The consent order requires Bank of America to hire an independent third party to review past transactions, identify suspicious activity that the bank failed to detect at the time, and report those transactions to FinCEN. "Financial crime compliance is serious, and we are responsible for getting it right," said a Bank of America spokesperson in a statement. "We have invested billions of dollars in technology and dedicated thousands of employees to combat financial crime, and our team is far along with and committed to completing the work required to address the issues raised by our regulators." The spokesperson added that the bank's third-quarter results due for release on Wednesday will include a non-tax-deductible charge of $1.2 billion, which will reduce quarterly net income by approximately 17 cents a share. Analysts have estimated adjusted EPS of $1.10, according to mean estimates compiled by LSEG, but that excludes one-offs like this fine. Shares were down 2.7% in after-hours trading after closing the day down 1.1%. The penalty is likely to add to negative investor sentiment and raise concerns about higher expenses and whether Bank of America can maintain its roughly $6 billion quarterly share buyback pace, UBS analyst Erika Najarian said in a note. With earnings due on Wednesday, "we think shares likely underperforming at open," she said. She noted there was no asset cap, a regulatory penalty that would limit how large the bank could grow. REGULATOR SAYS COMPLIANCE PROGRAM 'DEFICIENT AND INEFFECTIVE' As part of the fine, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency levied a $750 million civil penalty against the lender, the largest ever for the regulator, citing failures to address shortcomings in its anti-money laundering programs that were identified as part of a 2024 cease-and-desist order from the watchdog. The regulator said the bank's compliance program was "deficient and ineffective," and its transaction monitoring system caused the bank to delay filing suspicious activity reports on billions of dollars of transactions. In addition, the bank paid an $11.6 million fine to the Office of Foreign Assets Control for over 400 apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs. The Treasury said the bank mistakenly processed millions of dollars in payments that violated sanctions programs targeting countries including Russia and Iran. The fine comes days after American Express [USN:L6N45U1AT TEXT:"was also hit with a $350 million penalty"] for similar anti-money laundering shortcomings.

item.title: Lightspeed cuts 250 roles by laying off staff, not filling vacancies
item.description: Lightspeed Commerce Inc. says 250 roles will be impacted as the company lays off staff and opts to not fill some vacancies.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: Lightspeed Commerce Inc. says 250 roles will be impacted as the company lays off staff and opts to not fill some vacancies. The Montreal-based software business says the cuts are meant to simplify its operations and create room to reinvest in customer growth and product innovations. Spokesperson Stéphanie Princivil did not answer questions about what areas of the company the layoffs and removal of vacancies targeted but said in an email that Lightspeed will provide more information when it reports quarterly earnings next month. Lightspeed has made several staffing cuts over the last few years as Dax Dasilva, Lightspeed’s founder and chief executive, returned to the top job. In hopes of creating more shareholder value, the company also conducted a strategic review, but it concluded last year with no go-private transaction. Instead, the company opted to double down on its North American retail and European hospitality divisions and sell Upserve, a business it owned which offered restaurant management tools. --- Tara Deschamps, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 13, 2026.

item.title: 年内追加利上げ適切、インフレなお高水準＝米ボストン連銀総裁
item.description:
Michael S. Derby
[ニューヨーク １３日 ロイター] - 米ボストン地区連銀のコリンズ総裁は１３日、な...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
年内追加利上げ適切、インフレなお高水準＝米ボストン連銀総裁 5:29 配信

４月１４日撮影　 REUTERS/Evan Vucci

Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク １３日 ロイター] - 米ボストン地区連銀のコリンズ総裁は１３日、なお高水準にあるインフレ率を押し下げるため、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は年内に追加利上げを実施する必要があるとの考えを示した。

コリンズ氏はボストン連銀開催の銀行会議向けの講演で、連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）が９月の会合で決定した利上げを支持したとした上で、「インフレ率を適時かつ持続的にＦＲＢが目標とする２％に戻すために、年末までに金利を若干引き上げることが適切になる」と述べた。

その上で、追加的な政策対応の必要性と、その適切な時期についての見方は、今後発表される一連の経済指標が見通しやリスクバランスに及ぼす影響に大きく左右されると指摘。経済と労働市場が堅調に推移していることから、ＦＲＢはインフレ目標の達成に政策運営の重点を置くことができると述べた。

経済見通しについては全体的に楽観的な見方を示したものの、いくつかのリスク要因が存在すると指摘。「最も可能性が高いシナリオは、労働市場がほぼ完全雇用の状態を維持する中で、国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）が健全な成長を続けるというものだ」とし、「このシナリオの下では、継続的な効率化の進展が需要と供給の均衡を支え、ディスインフレに寄与することで、インフレ率は徐々に２％に低下する」と述べた。

同時に、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連インフラの整備に向けた技術投資の拡大のほか、関税の影響、中東での戦争を背景としたエネルギーコスト上昇で、インフレ抑制に向けた取り組みが複雑化する可能性があると警告。「ジェット燃料やディーゼル（軽油）、暖房用燃料油など精製エネルギー製品の価格が最近上昇していることを踏まえると、総合インフレ率とコアインフレ率はいずれも向こう数カ月にわたりＦＲＢの２％目標を上回って推移する可能性がある」との見方を示した。

ＦＲＢは９月１５─１６日のＦＯＭＣで０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決定。決定は全会一致で、利上げは２０２３年７月以来、３年２カ月ぶりだった。同会合で公表されたＦＯＭＣ参加者の金利見通しでは、年末までにあと１回の追加利上げが示された。複数のＦＲＢ当局者はここ数週間、追加利上げは今月２７─２８日の会合ではなく、その次の１２月の会合で決定されるとの見方を強く示唆している。

コリンズ総裁は今年のＦＯＭＣで投票権を持っていない。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：サービス価格上昇に加速の気配、日銀の緩和修正判断に影響も コラム：前途開けた中国人民銀行、「バズーカ砲」不要か コラム：3月のマイナス解除、否定しなかった植田総裁会見の本音 コラム：日銀金融政策の「その先」、政策金利が中立化した後の課題とは＝井上哲也氏 コラム：ウォーシュ氏、問われる「有言実行」　市場の信頼回復は道半ば 最終更新: 10/14(水) 5:29 ロイター

item.title: Televisa, Fintech to take on America Movil with $2 billion purchase of AT&T's Mexican unit
item.description: Grupo Televisa , and Fintech Holdings have agreed to buy AT&T's Mexican unit for $2 billion in cash, setting up a showdown with telecoms giant America Movil and marking one of Mexico's biggest M&A deals in recent years.
item.dc:creator: Iñigo Alexander
item.content:encoded: Grupo Televisa (TLEVISACPO.MX) , and Fintech Holdings have agreed to buy AT&T's (T.N) Mexican unit for $2 billion in cash, setting up a showdown with telecoms giant America Movil (AMXB.MX) and marking one of Mexico's biggest M&A deals in recent years. News of the deal, described as a "bargain" by Scotiabank, sent shares in Televisa, Mexico's largest broadcaster and the world's largest producer of Spanish-language content, surging 5% in after-hours trading on the New York Stock Exchange. AT&T's Mexican unit, the country's second-largest mobile operator after America Movil's Telcel, had some 24.7 million subscribers as of December, Televisa said. The deal will give Televisa considerable scale, lifting its share of total fixed and wireless subscribers in Mexico to 19% from 8%, according to the Scotiabank note to clients. "We think the low price tag and Fintech involvement is, in itself, bad news for (America Movil), as it means the new owners can focus more resources in capex," Scotiabank said. Fintech, a private investment firm and holding company owned by the Mexican billionaire David Martinez, owns 22.3% of Televisa and will take a 50% stake in the purchasing consortium. It is Televisa's second attempt to enter the competitive telecommunications sector, after an unsuccessful effort between 2012 and 2014. Despite Mexico's large population, its proximity to the US, and growing demand for connectivity, establishing a foothold in the sector has long proven a challenge due to high costs and fierce competition from Telcel. Scotiabank said the new venture could seek a direct-to-cell partnership with operators like Starlink to compete with Telcel, which operates twice as many connectivity towers and runs a much stronger 5G network throughout the country. For AT&T, the sale will allow it to concentrate on its US fiber and 5G businesses, as it pours more resources into "advanced connectivity" for an AI-enabled future. Shares in AT&T gained 1.6% to close at $22.85. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending regulatory approvals in Mexico. The price is subject to adjustments, plus additional contractual and contingent benefits, and will be funded through available cash and non-recourse secured debt financing, Televisa said. AT&T is not the only company to depart the Mexican telecoms sector. Spanish telecoms giant Telefonica Movistar in April [USN:L6N40R03P TEXT:"sold its Mexico business"] to a US-led consortium for $450 million as it shifts its focus onto core markets in Europe. AT&T's Mexican unit ended 2025 with revenue of 85.4 billion pesos ($4.65 billion) and operating income of 1.4 billion pesos, Televisa said. ($1 = 18.36 Mexican pesos)

item.title: Cornell bans fraternity parties for rest of academic year after alleged gang rape
item.description: The measure is the strongest reaction yet from Cornell's leadership to a lawsuit filed by a former undergraduate alleging seven men sexually assaulted her during a party.
item.dc:creator: Maria Tsvetkova
item.content:encoded: Cornell University will ban parties and social events at fraternity houses until the end of the academic year, its president said on Tuesday, responding to the outcry over an alleged gang rape on campus in 2024. The measure is the strongest reaction yet from Cornell's leadership to a lawsuit [USN:L1N45T0PE TEXT:"filed by a former undergraduate"], Jane Doe, alleging seven men sexually assaulted her during a party. Over the last several weeks, the Ivy League school in Ithaca, New York, and its president, Michael Kotlikoff, have come under heavy criticism from students, faculty and donors over its response to the allegations. The suspension of parties and social events will apply to Interfraternity Council houses. The council website says Cornell currently has 34 fraternity houses. "These measures will provide time for a thorough review of fraternity life at Cornell to determine whether and how it can safely continue," Kotlikoff said in the statement. The Cornell Interfraternity Council did not immediately reply to a request for comment. Prosecutors reopened the investigation into the alleged gang rape after the lawsuit was filed. New York state Governor Kathy Hochul appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James as an independent special prosecutor in the case, citing the earlier failure to protect the alleged victim. President Donald Trump repeated on Tuesday his call to take James, his longtime critic and an elected Democrat, off the case. "The Governor should take James off this case, immediately," Trump posted on Truth Social. Trump first questioned James' appointment in early October, but his comments did not prompt any action by officials. The offices of Hochul and the attorney general did not immediately reply to requests for comment. Since the [USN:L1N45K0ML TEXT:"lawsuit"] against seven fraternity members, the university and others was filed in September, the Cornell administration has faced student protests, a pending no-confidence resolution from faculty, criticism by alumni and a public assembly where students blamed university officials for tolerating what they described as a culture of sexual violence. None of the men named in the lawsuit have been criminally charged. "I have spent the past weeks listening to students, faculty, staff, parents, alumni, and trustees, who have shared their feelings of deep connection and sympathy with Jane Doe, anger and frustration that this could happen at Cornell," Kotlikoff said. "Women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe," he said, adding that additional staff would be hired to support survivors of sexual assault. Cornell will also work with New York State Police to investigate incidents, he said, and accelerate previous recommendations put forward by a task force on sexual violence. Thirty-five percent of undergraduate women reported experiencing non-consensual sexual contact involving force or incapacitation since entering Cornell, according to a university survey conducted in 2025 and published on its website. "We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action," Kotlikoff said.

item.title: Congo's confirmed Ebola cases exceed 9,000 as containment efforts falter
item.description: The Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, with the death toll approaching half the number of confirmed cases ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Congo's confirmed Ebola cases exceed 9,000 as containment efforts falter

Congo's confirmed Ebola cases exceed 9,000 as containment efforts falter The Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, with the death toll approaching half the number of confirmed cases

The outbreak has created new hot spots as it spreads to more communities, with 65 health zones across seven provinces now affected | Image: Bloomberg

AP Bunia (Congo) 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 14 2026 | 8:45 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Confirmed cases in Congo's Ebola outbreak have surpassed 9,000, with more than 4,300 deaths, as health authorities struggle to contain an outbreak spreading across seven provinces, according to government figures released Tuesday. The Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, with the death toll approaching half the number of confirmed cases. The rising death toll has alarmed health workers and authorities, with a large share of recorded deaths occurring outside treatment centres. The latest report recorded 88 new cases and warned that "community transmission remains a concern."   The outbreak has created new hot spots as it spreads to more communities, with 65 health zones across seven provinces now affected.

Officials say the confirmed cases account for only a third of all cases, with many going undetected. The outbreak involves the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Efforts to contain the virus have been impaired by several factors, including fighting between government forces and rebel groups, which has created one of the world's direst humanitarian crises, widespread disregard for health precautions, intense population movements and shortages of medical supplies and treatment centres. Also Read

Ebola outbreak in Congo spreads to new hotspots, health workers warn

Congo plane crash: 14 people killed, including 2 senior military officials

Congo school fire kills at least 26 students, injures dozens in Bukavu

Congo Ebola outbreak may be 3 times larger than official count: Africa CDC

Congo Ebola outbreak hits 5,000 cases as it outpaces response efforts

The outbreak has surpassed Congo's 16 previous outbreaks in scale and is on track to top the 2014-2016 West Africa regional outbreak that killed 11,000 people.

"I feel that the government is overwhelmed by events. But there is nothing else to say. The government needs to fully shoulder its responsibilities to ensure the effectiveness of the response against Ebola," said Samuel Buju, a resident of Bunia, the provincial capital of Ituri, one of the outbreak's hot spots. Last week, Kenya became the second country after Uganda to report an Ebola case imported from Congo, deepening concerns about the virus spreading across borders.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Sanaa as Houthi conflict escalates
item.description: The strikes marked a fresh escalation in the widening Middle East crisis and came shortly after a coalition spokesman urged residents to evacuate the area for their safety ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Sanaa as Houthi conflict escalates

Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen's Sanaa as Houthi conflict escalates The strikes marked a fresh escalation in the widening Middle East crisis and came shortly after a coalition spokesman urged residents to evacuate the area for their safety

| REUTERS

AP Cairo 5 min read Last Updated : Oct 14 2026 | 8:44 AM IST

Listen to This Article

A coalition of forces in Yemen led by Saudi Arabia carried out new airstrikes Tuesday on the Houthi rebel-held Yemeni capital of Sanaa, the Houthi-run broadcaster Al Masirah and residents said. The strikes marked a fresh escalation in the widening Middle East crisis and came shortly after a coalition spokesman urged residents to evacuate the area for their safety. Witnesses reported hearing strong explosions in Sanaa hours after the coalition struck the al-Suhaba fuel facility west of the city. In a rare statement earlier, the coalition had urged civilians in the Houthi-controlled capital to leave the Yemeni Oil Company site, on a hill overlooking the capital, and nearby storage areas ahead of a possible strike.

Houthi officials appeared to have anticipated the attack there. The oil company said its storage facilities were empty and that a Saudi strike would not affect oil reserves or supplies for residents. Still, witnesses in the city said lines of cars formed at some gas stations amid fears of a shortage. Shortly after the warning, Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said on Telegram that any Saudi attack on Sanaa would be met with a "firm and painful" response in the Saudi capital, Riyadh. Also Read

OpenAI employee arrested for planting hidden recording device in office

Houthis used Claude to develop missiles, test-fired rocket: Anthropic

Top oil executives dropped from WPC Energy Congress amid Houthi attacks

The untested promise of the Mecca alliance premium

Saudi Arabia has few options as Houthis aim at heart of its ambitions

It was unclear whether the Tuesday strike was a signal of military escalation or a carefully measured response to recent deadly attacks on the Riyadh airport.

The warning and the attack show "the Saudis' aims of upping the ante and striking deep in the heart of Houthi-controlled territory while attempting to control the narrative by presenting themselves as more careful and humanitarian actors than the Houthis," said Adam Baron, a fellow at the Washington-based New America Institute. "It may be a warning -- or it may be a sign of things to come," he said. Fighting surged over control of a key waterway Saudi Arabia is still scrambling to determine how its air defences failed to intercept a barrage of missiles and drones fired by the Houthis, including an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday that killed at least 13 people and wounded over 300.

The latest conflict between the Saudis and the Houthis began last month after the rebels seized key areas along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical waterway for the transport of Gulf oil and other goods at the southern end of the Red Sea off Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition, backing forces aligned with Yemen's internationally recognised government, has been trying to retake them. Saudi Arabia's Cabinet on Tuesday warned the Houthis they would "face consequences" for their repeated attacks on the kingdom. "The Kingdom will not allow any threat to its security or to freedom of maritime navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb Strait," the Cabinet said in a statement carried by Saudi state-owned Al-Ekhbariya television. The Bab el-Mandeb is another area key to the flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf.

The fight for a major Yemeni city On Tuesday, Yemen's interior ministry said in a statement on X that Houthi strikes over the past day on Taiz, a major city in the country's southwest, had killed six people and injured 18 amid ongoing battles in the region. A commander with the Saudi-backed forces said rebels had fought through fierce resistance to reach the edges of Taiz, and some had entered the city. The fight was now critical for Taiz, which has long been a sought-after prize, he said. The commander, speaking on condition of anonymity to describe battlefield details, said rebel forces were surprisingly large and bolstered by medium- and short-range ballistic missiles.

But he said the fighting was fiercest over control of the Kahboub mountains, which overlook Bab al-Mandeb and Aden, seat of the internationally backed government. The commander said his forces have called for reinforcements. Earlier Tuesday, the Houthis renewed their warning against using Saudi airspace, Houthi-controlled media reported. Several airlines have suspended service to the kingdom because of the Houthi attacks on airports. In a statement published by the Houthi-controlled SABA news agency, the Houthi-run foreign ministry referred to Saudi Arabia as the "Kingdom of the Horn of Satan" and said the kingdom "must realise that security, stability, and sovereignty must belong to everyone; otherwise, no one will enjoy them."   Meanwhile, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty called for the Houthis to immediately halt attacks on Saudi Arabia.

"There is no justification for these attacks, and they cannot be accepted," Abdelatty told Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in a phone call Tuesday. Abdelatty also called for prioritising diplomacy and a political solution to the conflict between Iran and the United States to avert "further escalation and instability" in the region, according to the Egyptian readout of the call. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier Tuesday that three drones had been intercepted north of Riyadh. The Associated Press couldn't independently verify that claim. Saudi Arabia has been pushing for the US military to provide more direct support in the fight against the Houthis.

The US has provided intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for a Saudi-led offensive, but has held off on carrying out strikes against the Houthis. A US intervention could prompt the Houthis to try to halt shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Stelco president responds to demands from Minister Joly
item.description: Stelco Inc. says Canadian exports of cold-rolled and coated steel to the United States have plunged 58 per cent compared with pre-trade-war levels, while continued foreign imports put pressure on ...
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — Canadian exports of cold-rolled and coated steel to the United States have plunged 58 per cent from pre-trade-war levels as foreign imports continue to undercut Canadian-made steel, Stelco Inc.’s president said in defending plans to lay off up to 500 workers across two Ontario plants. In a seven-page letter to Canada’s industry minister obtained by The Canadian Press, Paul Simon described an industry upended by U.S. tariffs, weakening demand and continued foreign steel imports. “Stelco cannot continue to produce cold-rolled and coated steel products without incurring significant losses that are not sustainable,” Simon said in the letter. “As such, we will continue with the idling of Hamilton Works.” The Oct. 9 letter provides new figures illustrating what Stelco says is a contracting market for its products. Canadian exports of cold-rolled and coated steel to the United States fell by 226,000 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026 compared with the 2024 quarterly average before the trade war began, Simon said. Meanwhile, imports accounted for 45 per cent of market share for those products, despite Ottawa’s efforts to protect domestic producers by restricting steel imports, he said. Simon argued that existing Canadian trade protections are “woefully inadequate” to create a sustainable market that can support two domestic producers of those products. Meanwhile, disruptions to Canadian industries that rely on cold-rolled and coated steel have led to a 10 per cent decline in domestic demand for those products, he said. The letter came in response to Industry Minister Mélanie Joly’s demand that Stelco explain how it will honour employment commitments made by its U.S.-based owner, Cleveland-Cliffs, when it acquired the company in 2024.  Ottawa’s approval of the takeover was contingent on Cleveland-Cliffs maintaining at least the same number of unionized workers and the vast majority of non-unionized employees for five years. Simon, who is also Stelco’s general counsel, said the company is proceeding with plans to idle its Hamilton finishing operations despite Joly’s warning of possible legal action. He argued that the layoffs, which are expected to impact both the Hamilton Works and Lake Erie Works plants, do not violate the company’s binding employment commitments, which he argued do not prohibit layoffs or require employment levels to remain above a specified number every day of the five-year period. Simon said Ottawa was warned as early as July that Stelco might indefinitely idle its Hamilton finishing operations, and that federal officials subsequently suggested discussions about revising the company’s employment commitments to reflect the planned shutdown and layoffs. In a statement posted to X on Oct. 10, Joly said Stelco’s employment commitments remain in force despite changing business strategies or market conditions, adding that all options remain on the table as government lawyers review the company’s response.  Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves has publicly supported U.S. steel tariffs while advocating for a “Fortress North America” approach that would see Canada and the United States impose stronger restrictions on steel imports from outside the continent. Joly had previously said Stelco has “explicitly chosen not to seek support” from government programs designed to preserve jobs and maintain operations. Simon said Ottawa’s offer of financial help did not address the underlying reasons for Stelco’s decision to idle some operations. He said the government offered funding to offset maintenance and capital expenses in exchange for retaining workers, but argued that the assistance would not solve the company’s lack of orders for cold-rolled and coated steel. He characterized the proposal as “a last-ditch effort to cover for an inadequate Canadian trade regime.” Stelco said it is taking steps to ensure its Hamilton finishing operations can restart with “minimal additional costs and time,” but provided no timetable for doing so. --- Brett Bundale, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 13, 2026.

item.title: Glencore shares trade higher on ASX debut as investors eye copper
item.description: Glencore's , shares started trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on Wednesday at a small premium to their London close, as the miner and trader hopes to secure a better valuation from investors seeking greater copper exposure.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Burton
item.content:encoded: Glencore's (GLEN.L) , shares started trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on Wednesday at a small premium to their London close, as the miner and trader hopes to secure a better valuation from investors seeking greater copper exposure. Glencore CEO Gary Nagle expects strong demand from Australian investors betting on copper's role in [USN:L8N45U2BV TEXT:"electrification"], he said on Friday, as demand rises for the metal's use in power grid expansions, transport and AI data centres. “Glencore has been investing in Australia for decades and we know the Australian investment community has a sophisticated understanding of global resources and commodity markets,” Nagle said in a statement on Wednesday. Glencore CHESS Depositary Interests (CDIs) opened at A$11.44 ($7.99), or 603 pence. On Tuesday, Glencore closed at 582.90 pence on the London Stock Exchange. The Switzerland-based company's CDIs are trading in a market home to other large miners like BHP Group (BHP.AX) , Rio Tinto (RIO.AX) , (RIO.L) and Fortescue <FMG.AX>, whose shares all edged down in early trading. Glencore shares already trade in London with another secondary listing in Johannesburg. Nagle has previously said he believes the $88 billion company can achieve inclusion in Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index (.AXJO) within 12 months, but analysts see momentum behind the stock potentially propelling it into the top indexes in [USN:L4N3Z11V1 TEXT:"half that time"]. "It is not every day that a company of Glencore’s scale joins the ASX, particularly in a period of subdued listing activity," said Paul Schroder, a partner at law firm Mallesons. "Its arrival is a significant addition to the Australian market and reinforces the ASX’s standing as a leading resources exchange." BUYOUT OPPORTUNITIES Analysts and investors speculated Glencore's decision to list Down Under could help acclimatise those [USN:L8N44B03D TEXT:"who had not seen value"] in its approach to Rio Tinto last year. Rio Tinto walked away from takeover talks with Glencore in February, ending months of negotiations over a $240 billion tie-up that would have reshaped the global mining industry. Nagle told reporters last week that a deeper local presence in Australia, where it produces coal, copper, zinc, lead and nickel, may [USN:L8N45U2BV TEXT:"yield business opportunities"], although it had no set buyout list. JPMorgan analysts said on Friday after a meeting with Nagle that Glencore's management team still saw merits in a combination with Rio Tinto and noted its shares had outperformed its Anglo-Australian rival by 10% since negotiations collapsed in February. "M&A is seen as part of the growth strategy and it was noted 'who knows what happens in the future,'" the analysts said in a report. ($1 = 0.7546 pounds, 1.4320 Australian dollars) (1 British pound = 1.8988 Australian dollars)

item.title: FBI arrests Saudi OpenAI engineer over covert recording device, DOJ says
item.description: The case highlights growing security concerns around sensitive AI research.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: US federal agents arrested a Saudi national who was an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company, the Justice Department said on Tuesday. The case highlights growing security concerns around sensitive AI research as companies and governments compete fiercely for the talent and technology that could confer economic and strategic advantages. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, had worked as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, the Justice Department said in a statement. An email sent to an address associated with that name did not elicit a response, and it was not immediately clear who his lawyer was. OpenAI discovered the recording device plugged into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room at one of its San Francisco buildings on September 30, according to the department. The thumb-sized device, which had a microphone and could connect to a camera, was concealed in toilet paper, according to an FBI complaint. It was installed on or about September 28, while its stored data was encrypted and inaccessible. Investigators later found a similar customized device in Alfozan's personal bag. OpenAI said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to identify the person responsible for planting the device and trace its origins. The company said it had evidence that the employee intended to place additional recording devices in sensitive areas of its offices to secretly record meetings. "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated," the company said. OpenAI referred the matter to the FBI, which is continuing to investigate. The Saudi embassy in the United States did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. "Abdulrahman Alfozan allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. Alfozan also used an AI productivity agent to seek information about meeting-room calendars and capabilities for about a month through September 16, according to the FBI complaint. He has been a legal permanent resident of the US since September 2020. If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine and three years of supervised release. A LinkedIn profile showed that Alfozan studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. He previously worked at Meta and Microsoft, it said. Reuters could not independently verify the details mentioned in his LinkedIn profile. Separately, the Information reported that OpenAI was in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits, a startup that identifies and fixes vulnerabilities in open-source software. The talks were ongoing and could fall apart, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. OpenAI and Trail of Bits did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. OpenAI said on Friday it fired three researchers after an investigation found they had violated company policies on handling sensitive information. The researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, had published a letter detailing the circumstances of their dismissal and arguing that the abrupt firings could create uncertainty among employees and undermine a culture in which researchers could raise safety concerns.

item.title: Oil prices rise as traders weigh Saudi supply risk, Russian diesel flow
item.description: Brent crude futures rose 89 cents, or 0.8%, to $106.58 a barrel by 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 80 cents, or 0.9%, to $94.94 ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / Commodities / Oil prices rise as traders weigh Saudi supply risk, Russian diesel flow

Oil prices rise as traders weigh Saudi supply risk, Russian diesel flow Brent crude futures rose 89 cents, or 0.8%, to $106.58 a barrel by 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 80 cents, or 0.9%, to $94.94

Brent fell 0.9% on Tuesday, while WTI rose 0.4%

Reuters TOKYO 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 14 2026 | 8:14 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Oil prices climbed on Wednesday as traders weighed supply risk from fighting between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and Saudi Arabia against the prospect of increased diesel from Russia. Brent crude futures rose 89 cents, or 0.8%, to $106.58 a barrel by 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 80 cents, or 0.9%, to $94.94. Brent fell 0.9% on Tuesday, while WTI rose 0.4%. "Supply concern stemming from conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia is driving prices higher," said chief strategist Hiroyuki Kikukawa at Nissan Securities Investment, a unit of Nissan Securities. "However, the expectation that increased Russian diesel exports will ease market tightness is likely to limit sharp price movement in either direction," Kikukawa said, projecting WTI to trade between $90 to $100 a barrel.

The Houthis attacked an administrative building belonging to state-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco in the city of Dhahran, causing a limited fire, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on Wednesday. Also Read

Oil volatility to rise ahead of midterm; Brent may test $120: Analyst

Record FPI outflows top ₹3 trillion in CY26, nearly double 2025 tally

Oil dips as Russia diesel supply prospects counter Gulf supply risks

A Nobel for shocks premium

Goldman ups Dec'26 oil forecast to $90/bbl; 2027 worst-case pegged at $125

The group has fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia over the past week in retaliation for the kingdom's support of Yemeni government forces. Riyadh's international airport has been hit four times, with a strike on Saturday killing 13 people. Last month, Saudi Arabia raised oil production despite disruption to shipments caused by the US-Iran war, leading to a sharp production increase from OPEC+ - the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and partners including as Russia - OPEC said on Tuesday.

Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships in the Strait of Hormuz to keep oil prices high and influence US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters. In Russia, the government said on Tuesday it did not see any direct link between peace talks with Ukraine and its deal to export diesel to the US. The comment came after Reuters reported that US envoys had told Ukrainian officials on Friday that the deal was part of an attempt to draw Russia back to negotiations for a peace settlement.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

Polish court to rule on custody of man suspected of plotting attack on PM

Reuters

13 October, 2026 11:30 pm IST

Facebook

WARSAW, Oct 13 (Reuters) – A Polish court will decide on Wednesday whether to keep in custody a man suspected of planning an attack on the prime minister and defence minister after improvised explosive materials were found in his apartment, prosecutors said.

The 66-year-old man, identified only as Krzysztof N. under Polish privacy law, was detained on Sunday on suspicion of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz.

He has been charged with nine offences, Warsaw regional prosecutors’ spokesperson Piotr Skiba told reporters on Tuesday.

Show Full Article

The man did not admit to the alleged offences and refused to provide an explanation.

“The most serious charge concerns plotting to forcibly overthrow state authorities — including the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers — using explosives stockpiled by the man,” Skiba said. He added that the suspect faces a prison sentence of 2 to 15 years for the offence if found guilty.

The other charges relate to recordings published online and include promoting an ideology advocating the violent seizure of power in Poland, promoting war including the one in Ukraine, and inciting crimes motivated by nationality, ethnicity, race or political views.

Skiba said the man had been seeking people to join his plans and had created a group comprising several hundred people, according to a recording reviewed by investigators.

While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is politically polarised and has faced heightened security concerns because of its proximity to the Russian war in neighbouring Ukraine.

The suspect was planning an attack on members of the current government, though he also criticised politicians from previous governments, Skiba said.

(Reporting by Anna Koper; Editing by Emelia Sithole-Matarise)

item.title: 'Gift to our adversary': More Republicans criticize Trump's Russia diesel deal
item.description: The lawmakers' letter to Trump said the agreement provides Russian President Putin's government with more fuel to finance its war, and will not benefit Americans.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle, Valerie Volcovici
item.content:encoded: A dozen US senators, including six Republicans, called on President Donald Trump on Tuesday to rescind his diesel deal with Russia , days before his administration must decide whether to formally impose new sanctions on Moscow over its war in Ukraine. The lawmakers' letter to Trump said the agreement provides Russian President Vladimir Putin's government with more fuel to finance its war , and will not benefit Americans, adding to a torrent of congressional criticism since Trump announced the deal on Friday. The resistance marks a shift from what had been Republicans' near-unanimous support for Trump's foreign policy decisions, weeks before November 3 midterm elections that will determine whether the party retains control of Congress. In his post, Trump said he was lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports, and that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons (2.25 million barrels) of diesel to US and global markets. Although Trump said he wanted to reduce prices, the amount he referenced is less than a day's supply for the US transport sector alone, according to US Energy Information Administration data, which shows daily use of around 2.94 million barrels per day. "Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin's murderous, illegal war," the lawmakers said in their letter. "This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded," they said. The senators' letter, dated Tuesday, was signed by Republicans Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, Thom Tillis of North Carolina, Susan Collins of Maine, Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and John Cornyn of Texas, as well as six Democrats. GRAHAM SANCTIONS BILL DEADLINE LOOMS Under [USN:L1N4570ZO TEXT:"a law"] Trump signed last month, he faces an October 18 deadline to impose sweeping new sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy over the Ukraine war, or waive them because he has determined that doing so is in the national interest. The letter urged Trump to execute the sanctions authorities included in the new law, called the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026", in honor of the late senator, a Russia hawk and close Trump ally who died in July. The administration has not yet told lawmakers whether it would impose the sanctions or issue a waiver. Collins, Murkowski and Tillis had joined Democrats in a [USN:O8N43T024 TEXT:"joint statement"] on Sunday calling on Trump to "reverse course" on [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"the deal"], saying it runs counter to US law barring imports of energy until Russia ends its aggression against Ukraine. Earlier on Tuesday, the Republican president [USN:S0N435010 TEXT:"was asked"] whether anyone had told him Russia could use proceeds of the diesel deal to purchase more bombs. "No, nobody told me anything," Trump responded, adding the deal benefited not just the US but the world. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak [USN:S8N45E0D7 TEXT:"said on Monday"] that Russia will be able to return diesel exports to levels above those Trump had outlined under the deal. The Democratic senators who signed the letter were Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Richard Durbin of Illinois, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Jack Reed of Rhode Island and Chris Coons of Connecticut.

item.title: Saudi Arabia plans hybrid format for marquee FII conference after attacks, sources say
item.description: Saudi Arabia plans to make its flagship investment conference a hybrid event, giving executives the option to tune in remotely, after deadly weekend attacks on Riyadh airport prompted a rethink of travel to the kingdom, said two people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia plans to make its flagship investment conference a hybrid event, giving executives the option to tune in remotely, after deadly [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"weekend attacks on Riyadh airport"] prompted a rethink of travel to the kingdom, said two people familiar with the matter. Some participants were still expected to fly in and could land at airstrips outside Riyadh, or even in neighbouring Gulf states, and then drive to the capital to attend the Future Investment Initiative scheduled for later this month, said one of the people. The Saudi government media office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Earlier this month organisers [USN:L8N45W01K TEXT:"said the event would go ahead"] despite missile attacks in the kingdom. Asked for comment, an FII media representative pointed Reuters to a statement from the CEO and chairman of the FII Institute sent before Saturday's attacks. "As we prepare to welcome thousands of delegates to Riyadh for the exceptional 10th edition of the Future Investment Initiative, their safety and well-being remain our highest priority," said CEO Maha Al Saud and Richard Attias, chairman of the executive committee. 'DAVOS IN THE DESERT' Major oil bosses [USN:L6N45Y0GT TEXT:"dropped out of an international conference"] on Monday and a hybrid model would allow for more participants to take part. The move shows how Saudi Arabia is trying to maintain its push to attract global investment despite an [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"escalating war with the Houthis"] that has challenged its efforts to turn Riyadh into a hub for global events. The kingdom has used the FII to showcase its plans to diversify its economy from oil and attract foreign investments. The typical attendance of a large number of world leaders, corporate chieftains and financiers has led the event to be nicknamed "Davos in the desert," in a nod to the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Switzerland. Global financial titans, including Goldman Sachs (GS.N) CEO and Chairman David Solomon, Standard Chartered (STAN.L) CEO Bill Winters and Citi's CEO Jane Fraser, were scheduled to participate as speakers at the event, according to a draft programme on the FII website dated October 6. Citi (C.N) and Goldman Sachs declined to comment on the executives' attendance, while Standard Chartered had no immediate comment. The FII event, in its 10th edition, is due to be held at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Centre, on the western edge of Riyadh.

item.title: Russia detains Japanese journalist on suspicion of spying
item.description: Russia's FSB security agency said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist for alleged espionage, and Moscow's Foreign Ministry said it regretted that Tokyo was using correspondents to carry out spying.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's FSB security agency said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist for alleged espionage, and Moscow's Foreign Ministry said it regretted that Tokyo was using correspondents to carry out spying. In a statement on its website, the FSB said the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper journalist was detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region on the day before he planned to leave Russia. It did not specify when this was. Russia and Japan, which never signed a formal World War Two peace treaty, have seen their diplomatic relations deteriorate since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, though Japan relies on Russia for supplies of liquefied natural gas (LNG). In a statement, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova identified the journalist as Imai Yuki, according to the Russian transliteration of his name, and said his detention cast a new pall on relations with Tokyo. Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi said on Wednesday that Japan's embassy in Moscow and consulate-general in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk had asked Russian authorities for information and called for fair treatment and humanitarian consideration for the Japanese national. Motegi did not confirm the identity of the person detained. The Hokkaido Shimbun said it was still confirming the details. "We will respond with the reporter's safety as our top priority," a spokesperson for the publisher said, declining to comment further. In a Russian state TV video report on the case, three masked men in black uniforms handcuffed a man lying on the ground as a voice off camera said he was suspected of spying. The video showed the man being accompanied by two FSB servicemen onto a plane, then in a cage in a Moscow court, which ordered him detained for nearly two months. The agency "thwarted the illegal activity" of the journalist, the FSB said. "As a result of intelligence operations, it was established that he gathered and stored information related to the country's defence capabilities in order to pass it on for national intelligence purposes to be used against the security of the Russian Federation," the statement said. "Tokyo's attempts to use its correspondents in Russia with the status of foreign journalists to gather information for undermining our state's security are regrettable," the foreign ministry spokeswoman said. Japan, she said, had adopted an anti-Russian position during Russia's military campaign in Ukraine and refused to consider Moscow's concerns about Tokyo's "remilitarisation". "We have to note that what has occurred will become an additional factor clouding the atmosphere of Russian-Japanese relations," Zakharova said. LONG-RUNNING DISPUTES Russia regards Japan as an [USN:L8N3ZG0NU TEXT:""unfriendly" country"] because it joined Western sanctions against Moscow over the war in Ukraine. Russia and Japan have a territorial dispute over the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories. Russian President Vladimir Putin [USN:L8N44F0CG TEXT:"visited"] one of the disputed islands in August, causing uproar in Japan. A delegation from China's Heilongjiang province also visited the island on Tuesday, amid strained relations between Beijing and Tokyo. Japan has said it would continue implementing sanctions against Russia and supporting Ukraine. This month, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's Cabinet approved additional sanctions against Russia, including expanded export bans and asset freezes targeting individuals affiliated with the Russian military. Asked whether improving US-Russia relations and Japan's reliance on energy imports from Russia made it difficult for Tokyo to take countermeasures, Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said: "It is true that there are many issues between Japan and Russia. "From Japan's perspective, despite the difficult situation in Japan-Russia relations, Japan has taken resolute measures based on its position. At the same time, Russia is a neighbouring country to Japan, and communication is necessary to resolve these issues." One of the most prominent cases of a foreign journalist arrested in Russia was the detention of [USN:L8N45H0MA TEXT:"Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich"] in 2023. He was found guilty of espionage by a Russian court, sentenced to 16 years and then freed in an East-West prisoner swap in August 2024.

item.title: Hyundai Motor Group bets $15.5 billion on India as global auto hub
item.description: Hyundai Motor Group said on Tuesday it would invest $15.5 billion in India through 2032, deepening its bet on the world's third-largest car market as a key driver of future growth.
item.dc:creator: Surbhi Misra, Nishit Navin
item.content:encoded: Hyundai Motor Group (005380.KS) said on Tuesday it would invest $15.5 billion in India through 2032, deepening its bet on the world's third-largest car market as a key driver of future growth. The South Korean automaker's seven-year plan includes about $700 million of investment in its Indian research and development centre, expansion of production capacity and a dedicated investment entity. India, the world's third-largest car market, is attracting billions of dollars in investment from global automakers seeking to tap rising demand and expand local manufacturing capacity, underscoring its position as a major automotive production hub. Hyundai said last year it would [USN:L3N3VW05E TEXT:"invest "]$5 billion to expand its manufacturing and research operations in India. Japan's Suzuki Motor (7269.T) , the majority owner of India's largest carmaker by volume, Maruti Suzuki, also laid out [USN:L4N3UI0G4 TEXT:"plans "]in 2025 to invest about $8 billion in the country. Carmakers such as Toyota and Honda have [USN:L4N3WC02H TEXT:"committed "]to expanding their manufacturing ambitions in India as well. Hyundai Motor, which employs more than 24,000 people in India, said the investment would create additional jobs across manufacturing, research, engineering and supply chains, but did not disclose a number. The firm said the investment plan, covering 2026 to 2032, would expand manufacturing capacity at Hyundai Motor India and Kia India to support significant volume growth. The investment also includes a vehicle testing track, as part of efforts to develop next-generation automotive technologies. The investment announcement followed a meeting between Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday. The group currently has an annual production capacity of more than 1.4 million vehicles in India, comprising 824,000 units at Hyundai's Chennai facilities, 170,000 units at its Pune plant and 431,000 units at Kia's Anantapur facility.

item.title: Wall Street banks see deals slow on market jitters but pipeline is strong
item.description: Wall Street's investment banking and trading stalwarts posted uneven third quarter earnings as both equity and bond markets were rocked by the ongoing Iran war, rising inflation and jitters about the massive spending in the AI buildout.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street's investment banking and trading stalwarts posted uneven third quarter earnings as both equity and bond markets were rocked by the ongoing Iran war, rising inflation and jitters about the massive spending in the AI buildout. The results from JPMorgan (JPM.N) , Citigroup (C.N) , Goldman Sachs (GS.N) and Wells Fargo (WFC.N) suggest a dealmaking and trading boom [USN:L6N43F12X TEXT:"that powered record first-half earnings"] may be slowing as a grinding bond market rout and equities volatility weighed on activity, particularly in late September, executives said. Still, dealmaking for the third quarter was solid overall with a strong pipeline, while consumers, commercial borrowers and the broader economy remain in good shape, executives said. "The economy continues to be very, very resilient despite some of the headwinds," Goldman CEO David Solomon said on an analyst call. "We have an extraordinary tech supercycle. I think we have a regulatory environment that is really encouraging strategic activity ... I think it's a pretty good environment." A prolonged bond market selloff, which has driven yields around the world to multi-decade highs and put further pressure on stock market valuations, has interrupted dealmaking. [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"The IPO market"] has lost steam in recent weeks, threatening what could have been a banner year for that business. JPMorgan in particular said market volatility and the uncertain economic outlook dampened dealmaking and reduced [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"bond-market trading in recent months"], although its chief financial officer Jeremy Barnum told reporters the deals pipeline remained "very strong." During market turmoil, the gap between buyers and sellers can widen temporarily, but for the most part deals had been delayed rather than canceled, he continued. Analysts have likewise said the IPO market has [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"been selective, not shut"], and delayed offerings could still launch if conditions stabilize during the fourth quarter, a sentiment Solomon echoed. "You might choose to wait, but the IPO market is still in pretty good shape," Solomon said. Citigroup CFO Gonzalo Luchetti [USN:FWN45Z0QV TEXT:"said the bank saw softer investment banking activity"] in the third quarter, while Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo also pointed to a September slowdown, noting on a call with reporters that the big jump in the benchmark 10-year yield has had an effect. "There is no doubt that high interest rates and the threat of continued Fed hikes is weighing on trading and IB activity in a measurably negative vector," said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management. Despite rising prices and borrowing costs, consumers and corporate borrowers remain resilient, with little deterioration in credit quality, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo executives said. "We're just not seeing anything that would imply that there's stress," said Santomassimo. EQUITY STRENGTH PERSISTS Banks also experienced strong trading in equities, as clients rejigged their portfolios on the back of rates uncertainty and surging energy prices. JPMorgan said revenue at its markets division climbed 15% in the third quarter from the prior year, with [USN:L4N45Z10B TEXT:"equity markets revenue surging 49%"]. Goldman beat third-quarter profit estimates, as volatile markets tied to the Middle East conflict[USN:L4N45Z111 TEXT:" lifted its equities revenue"], even as its fixed income, currency and commodities business revenue dropped [USN:L4N45Z111 TEXT:"1% from the year-earlier period"]. Shares were mixed after results, with Wells Fargo and Citigroup lower while JPMorgan and Goldman rose. "Our main concern with this and with other bulge bracket firms remains how much of the 'beats' seem concentrated in the equities trading business and how sustainable they will prove," said Chris Kotowski, analyst at Oppenheimer & Co, in a note.

item.title: Trump fires ambassador to Greece Guilfoyle after reports of misconduct
item.description: The White House said on Tuesday it had asked US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign after a series of news reports raised concerns she sold access to Trump administration officials in exchange for money, gifts and favors.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage , Edward Mcallister, Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: The White House said on Tuesday it had asked US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign after a series of news reports raised concerns she sold access to Trump administration officials in exchange for money, gifts and favors. US President Donald Trump had said on Monday that he was considering firing Guilfoyle, who was once engaged to his son Donald Trump Jr. On Tuesday, he told reporters: "She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading." US lawmakers had raised the alarm after a series of stories in the Wall Street Journal beginning last month that detailed Guilfoyle's conduct, including claims she threatened to use US influence to undermine the Greek government. New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia confirmed Guilfoyle had been asked to resign, telling a briefing: "She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well." In a post on X, Guilfoyle repeated denials of wrongdoing and said her gratitude and respect for Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio remained "unwavering." "While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end," she wrote. "These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity." One of the reports published by the Journal described Guilfoyle's close relationship with a lobbyist for a Greek energy company and her promotion of that firm, while another cited audio recordings of Guilfoyle bragging about her ties to wealthy Greek businessmen as she sought an invitation to a Davos dinner honoring another of Trump's sons, Eric. US businessman Eric Deters also told the newspaper that Guilfoyle, a former San Francisco prosecutor, had offered access to Trump administration officials for money, at one point asking him to pay her $100,000 credit card bill.Britain's Daily Mail reported last week that the State Department's internal watchdog was looking into complaints of inappropriate behavior from staff at the Athens embassy. The Greek government has not commented on the allegations involving her tenure as ambassador. Neither the State Department nor Washington's embassy in Athens responded to requests for comment. DEALS AND DIPLOMATIC WAVES Greece has been an important NATO ally of the United States, offering key military facilities to safeguard security in the Eastern Mediterranean, and it leads an EU maritime mission to protect commercial shipping in the Red Sea. During a visit to Athens last week, Rubio said Greece and the US were launching new counterterrorism information sharing between their law enforcement agencies. Guilfoyle's tenure in Athens was high profile from the start as she appeared on the cover of Vogue Greece and attended late-night parties with Greek celebrities. She aggressively touted American interests, including signing deals for the import of US liquefied natural gas and [USN:L6N3WI0FW TEXT:"drilling deals involving companies including Exxon Mobil"]. But she also created diplomatic waves. In her first interview with local media after arriving last November, she said China should sell its 67% stake in the port of Piraeus, which has become a cornerstone of Beijing's Belt and Road Initiative. China’s ambassador to Greece, Fang Qiu, responded by accusing the US of having "an outdated and a harmful mentality" and "a hegemonic mindset." Dimitris Mantzos, foreign affairs spokesperson for Greece’s opposition PASOK party, said Guilfoyle’s firing raised serious issues and unanswered questions. Would Greek officials demand an explanation, he said, or "content themselves with watching the country serve as a 'theater'" for outside interests.
